body:
Thanks for reporting!

Just to gather a bit more information, is there a change of behaviour when you set these two project settings:

1. Configure the [Display Server Driver.linuxbsd](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-display-display-server-driver-linuxbsd) advanced project setting to wayland
2. Turn on the [HDR 2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-rendering-viewport-hdr-2d) project setting

This should make no difference for this bug, but since it should be easy to test, it would be good to double check.

CC @ArchercatNEO

To build on that could you also run the HDR output sample project from https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects?

This should give the values for min/reference/max luminance (as relative values), which I suspect are breaking slightly. Godot expects the compositor to provide reference and max luminance values for HDR to work.

On the Hyprland side, I can't find how to set these two values but I expect it could have something to do with the `sdrbrightness` and `sdrsaturation` config values, have both of these been set? Godot doesn't support ICC profiles but if the previous settings don't work, maybe Hyprland is able to read ICC profiles and convert them into reference/maximum luminance.

UPDATE: https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/discussions/14682
Seems like hyprland has some undocumented `sdr_max_luminance` and `sdr_min_luminance` values. These combined with `sdrbrightness` should give correct HDR values. Though values reported by the monitor are often wrong, they shouldn't be so wrong as to break anything (this is why kde provides a configuration widget to find the true max luminance of the monitor but that's beside the point).

> To build on that could you also run the HDR output sample project from https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects?
> 
> This should give the values for min/reference/max luminance (as relative values), which I suspect are breaking slightly. Godot expects the compositor to provide reference and max luminance values for HDR to work.

This project should be used instead, which shows reference/max luminance: https://github.com/allenwp/godot-hdr-output-test-project

(The official demo project only shows reference and max luminance on Windows because this is a platform that allows configuring them inside the Godot game.)

@gatitorivera are you able to test HDR output on any other apps? It seems like this might be something that affects all HDR apps on hyperland that use the reference luminance (brightness) setting from Wayland, not just Godot. If that's the case then I think this issue can be closed, since this is not an issue specific to Godot. 

If the issue is specific to Godot and cannot be reproduced with other apps that render HDR output  like Blender, then we may consider adding a documentation note about it if it affects many users.

After digging a bit, it looks like Hyprland ignores `set_luminances` for `ext_linear` and assumes `1.0 = 80 nits` (instead of 10,000 nits). I've opened a discussion on their side for this: https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/discussions/16498

Godot's `set_luminances` request follows the protocol and works correctly on `KWin`.

Separately, on compositors that don't support `set_luminances` (e.g. wlroots/sway), Godot still normalises to the compositor's max, but the compositor assumes the protocol default of `1.0 = 80 nits`. From reading the source this would be dim there too, so falling back to `1.0 = 80 nits` in that case might be worth it (untested on sway).
